key_insight: Specialized ML force fields extend machine-learning interatomic potentials beyond near-equilibrium prediction by adding physics-driven adaptations for reactive, nonlocal, and highly strained materials dynamics.
engineering_relevance: For fracture and damage modeling, the paper argues that force fields must be chosen and validated against the specific observable of interest, not just general benchmark accuracy.
method: Assess MLIP design trade-offs: strained-state coverage, message-passing cost, and nonlocal interaction handling.
Map performance to four demanding settings: electrified interfaces, open systems, multiphase evolution, and large-scale fracture.
Compare universal foundation models with task-specific potentials using observable-specific benchmarks.
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes and evaluates evidence across four challenging application contexts to test whether specialized potentials remain accurate for the intended dynamical observables.
watch_item: Specialized models can fail outside their training distribution, and high-order or nonlocal architectures may introduce major computational overhead and hardware constraints.
paper_title: Specialized machine learning force fields for materials dynamics
